requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while working with composite materials and what you should do to anticipate, mitigate, prevent, and respond to these hazards. Describe the appropriate safety gear and clothing that should be used when working with composite materials. (b) Explain the precautions that must be taken when handling, storing, and disposing of resins, reinforcements, and other materials used in composites. Include in your discussion the importance of health, safety, and environmental responsibility and awareness. (c) Describe what a safety data sheet (SDS) is and tell why it is used.

pamphlet_excerpts: New Composites Industry: The new composites industry developed further during World War II.
Air Force Navy: The U.S. Air Force and Navy made good use ofthese properties of composites in many aircraft and watercraft.
Composites Grew Quickly: After the war, the use of composites grew quickly.
Boats Trucks Sports: Boats, trucks, sports cars, storage tanks, pipes, and ducts, almostanything imaginable, werebuilt using composites.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Review Standard (Req 2): Read the official Composite Materials requirement and identify the key questions, terms, or skills covered in Composite materials.
Step 2 - Gather Evidence & Examples: Research the required facts in the Composite Materials Pamphlet and record structured notes in your Scout Workbook.
Step 3 - Practice & Apply (Demonstrate): Work with your patrol buddy or family (as required) to demonstrate each element of Composite materials with concrete real-world examples.
Step 4 - Counselor Conference & Sign-Off: Present your completed workbook organizer and demonstrate your understanding to your Merit Badge Counselor for Blue Card verification.

requirements.lead_text: Describe how composite materials are made. Then do the following:
requirements.req_text: Describe how composite materials are made. Then do the following: (a) Discuss three different composite reinforcement materials, their positive and negative characteristics, and their uses. Obtain the SDS for each one and discuss the toxicity, disposal, and safe-handling sections for these materials. (b) Discuss three different resins used in composites, their positive and negative characteristics, and their uses. Obtain the SDS for each one and discuss the toxicity, disposal, and safe-handling sections for these materials. Include thermoset resins and thermoplastic resins in your discussion. (c) For each of the three resins you chose for requirement 3(b), think of a new application that might be worth developing.

pamphlet_excerpts: Resins Composites Thermoset: Resins used in composites can be either thermoset orthermoplastic.
Thermoset Resins Changed: Thermoset resins are changed from a liquid to a solid in an irreversible process calledcrosslinking.
Thermoplastic Resins Hand: Thermoplastic resins, on the other hand, can be remelted and recycled; the hardening processis reversible.
Thermoplastics Typical: Thermoplastics are the typical plastics we are familiar with athome and at school.
step_by_step_procedure: Includes Toys Plastic: This includes toys, plastic containers of alltypes, and hundreds of common items we use every day.
Common Thermoset Resins: Common thermoset resins include polyester, vinyl ester, andepoxy.
Polyester Resins Commonly: Polyester resins are the most commonly used because theyare low in cost and are suitable for many products.
Epoxy Resin Tough: Epoxy resin is tough, nonconductive, resistant to chemicals, and dimensionally stable.

pamphlet_excerpts: Large Composites Projects: In large composites projects, several pieces of fiberglassreinforcement might be necessary to cover the surface.
Join Pieces Fiberglass: When you join pieces of fiberglass reinforcementto form a seam, overlap the pieces by 1 to 3 inches.
Ensures Structural: This ensures that the structural properties of the laminate are not weakened.
Than Layerof Reinforcement: If you use more than one layerof reinforcement, be sure to stagger or space out theoverlaps to avoid thick buildups that also can createweak areas.
step_by_step_procedure: Saturate Fiberglass: When you saturate the fiberglass reinforcement with resin, air can be trapped in the laminate, creating voids.
Air Voids Aresimply: Air voids aresimply bubbles, which when trapped in the cured laminate cancause problems ranging from poor appearance to structuralfailure.
Squeegee Paint Rollerto: To remove air bubbles, use a squeegee or a paint rollerto push the saturated glass reinforcement evenly down to themold surface, squeezing air.
Temperature Properly Curing: Temperature is important in properly curing resins.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to the Composite Materials merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include—with your parent or guardian's permission—an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from the Composite Materials merit badge to pursue a hobby or interest. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

pamphlet_excerpts: Careers Composites Industry: Careers in the Composites Industry The composites industry offers many career opportunities.
Position Company Produces: You might find a position with a company that produces theraw materials used in manufacturing composites, or a companythat makes composite parts.
Youmight Work University: Youmight work at a university or in a laboratory doing research anddevelopment on new materials or processes.
Workin Design Creating: You might workin design, creating new applications for composite materials.
step_by_step_procedure: Further Education Training: Further education or training is necessary, however, for mostopportunities in the composites industry.
Educational Requirements: Educational requirements beyond high school depend onthe career path you choose.
Positions Require: Some positions require a two-yeartechnical or associate degree; others require a four-year bachelor’sdegree.
Advanced Positions Master: For advanced positions, you might need a master’s degreeor doctorate.
